tokens.source: orchestrator_usage (share of the FFT64/128 dispatch chain; FFT64 carries the earlier dispatches)

notes:
ALL ARITHMETIC VERIFIED ON CHIP; THE CROSSING IS NOT. Split after STAGE 0 (die 0 = 30 cells, the period-64 octant fold; die 1 = 84 cells, stages 1..6). The originally-planned stage-2 cut does NOT place — SHAPE, not area, is binding.

MEASURED SEPARATELY, so a whole-system failure is never attributed by guesswork:
  * die 0 alone: 80/80 BIT-EXACT on a real built chip vs sdf_streaming_reference(128, x, (0,0)), incl. 16 non-zero outputs past its delay-64 latency. This is the genuinely NEW arithmetic in FFT128 — the period-64 fold needing 16+16 octant tables where N=64 needs 8+8, the one stage with no N=64 counterpart.
  * die 1 alone: 200/200 BIT-EXACT, fed die 0's OWN output stream. Its layout hash is IDENTICAL to FFT64's (e27f020b27441656) and the DIF angle identity stage_table(128,s+1)==stage_table(64,s) means it computes the transform FFT64 already verified — but it was MEASURED, not asserted.
  * wired together through MultiChipSimulation: 0 of 520 words, livelocks from trigger 1.

THREE REAL ENGINE DEFECTS were found and fixed in the inter-chip build path along the way — all invisible to the shipped 2-chip GainBlock example, which is the only prior exerciser of that path — and it STILL livelocks, so at least one further fault remains. Marked needs_human with the boundary handshake flagged rather than shipping an unverified crossing.

COMPOSITION IDENTITY: the split is expressed as a STAGE_RANGE parameter on the same class, so both dies run identical builders/fold/planner as the verified single-die transform, and correctness reduces to whole(x) == die1(die0(x)) — asserted word-for-word over 511 samples x 3 seeds with INV-4 teeth (26/26 split gates green) rather than argued.

DURABLE LESSONS: 'a contract exercised by exactly one instance is not yet a contract' (the placer's bounding-box normalization was invisible until a second instance needed a non-(0,0) anchor; fixed via a declared anchor after the first fix destroyed die 0's only valid geometry); and 'a large number is not automatically conservative' (sim.run(400_000, 4000) is events-per-chip-per-round x rounds — an enormous budget, not a safe one; derived down to (20_000, 40), taking a 6-sample run from minutes to ~30s — the same class of error as the under-budgeted saturated gate, in the opposite direction).
